Capture guide →

FROM YOUR LAPTOP TO THE ANALYZER

Capture. Inspect. Explain.

A repeatable localhost exercise for your Theme E demonstration.

01

Choose loopback

Install Wireshark and Python 3.10+. In Wireshark choose Adapter for loopback traffic capture on Windows, lo on Linux or lo0 on macOS. Windows needs Npcap.

Set the capture filter, then start recording.

host 127.0.0.1 and (tcp port 8080 or udp port 9999 or icmp)
02

Generate your traffic

Download the local generator and run it on your laptop. It creates five HTTP requests and five UDP echo exchanges on your own computer.

Download generate_traffic.py ↓
python generate_traffic.py

Optional ICMP: Windows ping -n 2 127.0.0.1; Linux/macOS ping -c 2 127.0.0.1.

03

Save and open

Stop recording. Save as classic PCAP, then open it in PacketScope. If your file is PCAPNG, convert it first:

editcap -F pcap input.pcapng output.pcap

Renaming the extension alone does not convert a file. Live packet counts will differ from the sample.

04

Explain what you see

Identify the TCP handshake, the HTTP GET and 200 OK response, and the UDP request/reply pairs. Use these Wireshark display filters:

tcp.port == 8080TCP conversationhttp.requestHTTP requestudp.port == 9999UDP echoicmpPing packets

What this project supports

Classic PCAP version 2.4; Ethernet/VLAN, loopback, raw IPv4 and Linux cooked headers. IPv4 TCP, UDP, ICMP and single-segment HTTP/1 inspection. Up to 20 MB and 100,000 packets.

No IPv6 decoding, TCP or fragment reassembly, DNS decoding, TLS decryption, input checksum validation or attack detection. Unsupported and malformed frames remain visible. Capture only your own or explicitly authorized traffic.
